title: SharePoint: FAQ web part becomes non-AI, with AI FAQ generation in Copilot in SharePoint
summary: Hold: Restricted Content Discovery is incorrectly described as the only documented control over where the AI route appears; Microsoft also documents Site AI settings. The FAQ change, rollout notice, default state and listed control path and command are supported.

claims.claim: The FAQ web part will provide standard non-AI manual creation, editing and management of FAQs.
claims.quote: The SharePoint FAQ web part will provide a standard, non-AI experience for manually creating, editing, and managing FAQs.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Enabling Restricted Content Discovery on a site removes Copilot in SharePoint and AI actions from that site.
claims.quote: If it's enabled on a site, Copilot in SharePoint and AI actions don't appear on that site. This rule applies regardless of your other availability settings.

claims.claim: The control is at SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites. Select the site you want to configure. Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery for a site.
claims.quote:
Enable Restricted Content Discovery for a site
Use PowerShell
Open PowerShell as an administrator and run the following command:
Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is an existing site-level control, not a control specific to the FAQ change.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery is an existing setting that's respected. If it's enabled on a site, Copilot in SharePoint and AI actions don't appear on that site.
